You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All apples are mangoes. All mangoes are lemons. All lemons are kiwis. Conclusions: (I) All apples are lemons. (II) All mangoes are kiwis.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to
be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given
statements.
Statements:
All apples are mangoes.
All mangoes are lemons.
All lemons are kiwis.
Conclusions:
(I) All apples are lemons.
(II) All mangoes are kiwis.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
options.html: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
options.html: Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

(I) All apples are lemons → Follow (As all apples are mangoes and all mangoes are lemons. As wholes apples comes in mangoes which whole comes in lemons, therefore it is true.)

(II) All mangoes are kiwis → Follow (As all mangoes are lemons and all lemons are kiwis. As wholes mangoes comes in lemons which whole comes in kiwis, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.question: Which figure should replace the question mark (?) if the following series were to be continued?
questions.questionHtml: Which figure should replace the question mark (?) if the following series were to be continued?
questions.solution:
1) First box series:

First row corner elements interchange positions.

First two elements of third row and center element shift anticlockwise.

The rest of the elements shift anticlockwise. 

2) Second box series:

Third column elements shift to the corner opposite sides.

Second column elements shift anticlockwise.

First column elements shift to the corner opposite sides diagonally.

Top left corner element is replaced by new element.

questions.question: Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All pens are pages. Some pages are pins. Some pins are boards. Conclusions: (I) Some pins are pens. (II) Some boards are pages. (III) Some pens are boards.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true,
even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s
from the given statements.
Statements:
All pens are pages.
Some pages are pins.
Some pins are boards.
Conclusions:
(I) Some pins are pens.
(II) Some boards are pages.
(III) Some pens are boards.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows.
options.html: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows.

questions.solution:
​

Conclusions:

(I) Some pins are pens→ Does not follow (As all pens are pages and some pages are pins. So it is possible but not definite.)

(II) Some boards are pages → Does not follow (As some pages are pins and some pins are boards. So it is possible but not definite.)

(III) Some pens are boards → Does not follow (As all pens are pages, some pages are pins and some pins are boards. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, None of the conclusions follow.

questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
A + B means ‘A is the wife of B’.
A − B means ‘A is the son of B’.
A × B means ‘A is the husband of B’.
A ÷ B means ‘A is the father of B’.
Based on the above, how is P related to T if ‘P − Q + R ÷ S × T’?
questions.solution: Thus, P is T's husband’s brother or brother-in-law
